text:
sophie: quick alert from today's profile: host tokenization and parse are showing a p95 spike after the recent slab-pool change (~15% tail increase).
omar: stack shows tokenize_slab_alloc -> utf8_normalize -> parse_frames. Any memstats?
sophie: slab alloc rate increased 2.5x; workers hit recycle high-water and started temporary mallocs.
trent: that explains jitter. if pool saturates we should backpressure or reuse smaller caches.
sophie: microbench: pre-reserve + per-worker cap -> median tokenization down 0.25ms -> 0.08ms, p95 down ~28%. But naive pool without cap raised RSS by ~12% on density nodes.
omar: propose two steps: 1) add per-worker slab cap + recycle eviction window, 2) cheap ascii fastpath to skip expensive normalize when possible.
trent: also noticed coalescer mixes very short and long sequences which confuses kernel selector; we should add a batching flush if preproc backlog > 1.2ms.
ops-bot: ticket PERF-7760 created: "slab pool cap + ascii fastpath + batching flush" assigned to sophie,omar,trent.
sophie: will open PRs with benches and mem numbers. Watch kvcache hitrate as affinity changes.
trent: ok to deploy to 5% canary once PRs land.
sophie: thanks, small-win expected if we get p95 host parse under 1.2ms.
